progress are costs for projects in progress to upgrade or refurbish certain rigs in our existing fleet. Additionally, we include other capital maintenance purchase-orders that are open/in process. As these various projects are completed, the costs are then classified to their appropriate useful life category.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairments - Fiscal Year 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Consistent with our policy, we evaluate our drilling rigs and related equipment for impairment whenever events or changes in circumstances indicate the carrying value of these assets may exceed the estimated undiscounted future net cash flows. Our evaluation, among other things, includes a review of external market factors and an assessment on the future marketability of specific rigs&#x2019; asset group. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the second quarter of fiscal year 2020, several significant economic events took place that severely impacted the current demand on drilling services, including the significant drop in crude oil prices caused by OPEC+'s price war coupled with the decrease in the demand due to the COVID-19 pandemic. To maintain a competitive edge in a challenging market, the Company&#x2019;s management introduced a new strategy focused on operating various types of highly capable upgraded rigs and phasing out the older, less capable fleet. This resulted in grouping the super-spec rigs of our legacy Domestic FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;3 asset group and our FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;5 asset group creating a new "Domestic super-spec FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;" asset group, while combining the legacy Domestic conventional asset group, FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;4 asset group and FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;3 non-super-spec rigs into one asset group (Domestic non-super-spec asset group).  Given the current and projected low utilization for our Domestic non-super-spec asset group and all International asset groups, we considered these economic factors to be indicators that these asset groups may be impaired. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As a result of these indicators, we performed impairment testing at March 31, 2020 on each of our Domestic non super-spec and International conventional, FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;3, and FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;4 asset groups, which had an aggregate net book value of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$605.8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million. We concluded that the net book value of each asset group is not recoverable through estimated undiscounted cash flows and recorded a non-cash impairment charge of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$441.4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million in the Consolidated Statement of Operations for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2020. Of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$441.4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million total impairment charge recorded, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$292.4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$149.0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million was recorded in the North America Solutions and International Solutions segments, respectively. No further impairments were recognized in fiscal year 2020. Impairment was measured as the amount by which the net book value of each asset group exceeds its fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The most significant assumptions used in our undiscounted cash flow model include timing on awards of future drilling contracts, drilling rig utilization, estimated remaining useful life, and net proceeds received upon future sale/disposition. These assumptions are classified as Level 3 inputs by ASC Topic 820 Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures as they are based upon unobservable inputs and primarily rely on management assumptions and forecasts.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;In determining the fair value of each asset group, we utilized a combination of income and market approaches. The significant assumptions in the valuation are based on those of a market participant and are classified as Level 2 and Level 3 inputs by ASC Topic 820 Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of March 31, 2020, the Company also recorded an additional non-cash impairment charge related to in-progress drilling equipment and rotational inventory of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$44.9&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$38.6&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million, respectively, which had aggregate book values of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$68.4&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$38.6&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million, respectively, in the Consolidated Statement of Operations for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2020. Of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$83.5&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million total impairment charge recorded for in-progress drilling equipment and rotational inventory, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$75.8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$7.7&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million was recorded in the North America Solutions and International Solutions segments, respectively. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairment - Fiscal Year 2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the third quarter of fiscal year 2019, the Company's management performed a detailed assessment, considering a number of approaches, to maximize the utilization and enhance the margins of the domestic and international FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;4 asset groups. In June 2019, this assessment concluded that marketing a smaller fleet of these two asset groups would provide the best economic outcome. As such, the decision was made to downsize the number of domestic and international FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;4 drilling rigs, to be marketed to our customers, from&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;71&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;rigs to&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;20&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;domestic rigs and from&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;10&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;rigs to&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;8&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;international rigs and utilize the major interchangeable components of the decommissioned drilling rigs within these asset groups as capital spares for all of our remaining rig fleet. This reduced the aggregate net book values of the FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;4 asset groups as of June 30, 2019 from&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$317.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;to&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$107.5 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;for domestic rigs and from&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$55.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;to&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$47.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;for international rigs. Following the downsizing process, we performed a detailed study to optimize the quantities of capital spares and drilling support equipment required to support the future operations of our rig fleet going forward. These decisions and analysis resulted in a write down of excess capital spares and drilling support equipment, which had an aggregate net book value of&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$235.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, to their estimated proceeds to ultimately be received on sale or disposal based on our historical experience with sales and disposals of similar assets, resulting in an impairment of&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$224.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, which was recorded in our Consolidated Statement of Operations for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2019. Of the&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$224.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;total impairment charge recorded,&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$216.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$7.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; was recorded in our North America Solutions and International Solutions segments, respectively. The significant assumptions in the valuation are classified as Level 2 inputs by ASC Topic 820, Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Due to the downsizing of our domestic and international FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;4 asset groups, at June 30, 2019, we performed impairment testing on these two asset groups. We concluded that the net book values of the asset groups are recoverable through estimated undiscounted cash flows with a surplus. The most significant assumptions used in our undiscounted cash flow model include timing on awards of future drilling contracts, operating dayrates, operating costs, rig reactivation costs, drilling rig utilization, estimated remaining useful life, and net proceeds received upon future sale/disposition. The assumptions are consistent with the Company's internal forecasts for future years. Although we believe the assumptions used in our analysis are reasonable and appropriate and the probability-weighted average of expected future undiscounted net cash flows exceed the net book value for each of the domestic and international FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;4 asset groups as of June 30, 2019, different assumptions and estimates could materially impact the analysis and our resulting conclusion.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairments - Fiscal Year 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2018, after ceasing operations in Ecuador, we entered into a sales negotiation with respect to the six conventional rigs, within a separate international conventional rigs&#x2019; asset group, with net book values of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$20.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, present in the country, pursuant to which the rigs, together with associated equipment and machinery, were sold to a third party to be recycled. Certain components of these rigs, with an&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$8.5 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; net book value, that were not subject to the sale agreement&#160;were transferred to the United States to be utilized on other FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae;&lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; drilling rigs with high activity and demand. The sales transaction was completed in November 2018. We recorded a non-cash impairment charge within our International Solutions segment of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$9.2 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, which is included in Asset Impairment Charge on the Consolidated Statement of Operations for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2018. As a result, the remaining rig within the same asset group, not to be disposed of, was written down resulting in an additional impairment charge of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. The assets were recorded at fair value based on the sales agreement and as such are classified as Level 2 within the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Furthermore, during the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2018, within our North America Solutions segment, management committed to a plan to auction several previously decommissioned rigs during fiscal year 2019. As a result, we wrote them down to their estimated fair values. We recorded a non-cash impairment charge of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$5.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, which is included in Asset Impairment Charge on the Consolidated Statements of Operations for the fiscal year ended September 30, 2018. The assets were recorded at fair value based on the auction price and as such are classified as Level 2 of the fair value hierarchy.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Decommissioning&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;While the crude oil market imbalance is a global phenomenon, it has more acutely impacted the U.S. market as a result of storage limitations during the last two quarters of fiscal year 2020. The abruptness of and the overall size of the decrease in demand for refined products, such as gasoline and diesel, has created an abundance of supply for such products which has caused the inventory levels of crude oil and its related refined products to become greatly elevated, reaching the high end of storage capabilities. This has greatly reduced the need, or in some cases, entirely eliminated the ability of refineries to use crude oil as a feedstock. As such, exploration and production ("E&amp;amp;P") companies, our customers, may have limited opportunities to offload their production and even then, the selling price could be at very low, uneconomical prices. Consequently, some E&amp;amp;P companies have chosen to shut-in and stop production, not complete additional wells drilled and/or not drill any more wells until the market imbalance corrects and it is economical to resume production and drilling wells.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-bottom:10px;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the fiscal year ended September 30, 2020, we decommissioned &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Verdana,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;two&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; rigs and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;35&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; rigs from our legacy Domestic Conventional asset group and FlexRig&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;sup style="vertical-align:top;line-height:120%;font-size:6pt"&gt;&#xae; &lt;/sup&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;3 asset group, respectively. The reclassifications and the adjustments arising from the new leasing rules are therefore recognized in the opening balance sheet on October 1, 2019.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Upon the adoption of ASC 842, we recognized lease liabilities in relation to leases that had previously been classified as operating leases under the principles of ASC 840. These liabilities were measured at the present value of the remaining lease payments, discounted using the lessee&#x2019;s incremental borrowing rate as of October 1, 2019, as most of our contracts do not provide an implicit rate. instead, for contracts entered into before the transition date, we relied on our assessment in which we applied ASC 840 prior to the adoption date,&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; Additionally, ASC 842 provides lessors with a practical expedient, by class of underlying asset, to not separate lease and non-lease components and account for the combined component under ASC 606 when the non-lease component is the predominant element of the combined component. The lessor practical expedient is limited to circumstances in which the lease, if accounted for separately, would be classified as an operating lease under ASC 842.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:left;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;With respect to our drilling service contracts that commenced or were amended during the fiscal year ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we concluded that our drilling contracts contain a lease component and that the non-lease component is the predominant element of the combined component of such contracts. As such, we elected to apply the practical expedient to not separate the lease and non-lease components and account for the combined component under ASC 606. Therefore, we do not expect any change in our revenue recognition patterns or disclosures as a result of our adoption of ASC 842.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Due to the market conditions described in &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span 2020, we concluded that goodwill and intangible assets might be impaired and tested the H&amp;amp;P Technologies reporting unit, where the goodwill balance is allocated and the intangible assets are recorded, for recoverability. This resulted in a goodwill only non-cash impairment charge of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$38.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; recorded in the Consolidated Statement of Operations during the fiscal year ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The recoverable amount of the H&amp;amp;P Technologies reporting unit was determined based on a fair value calculation which uses cash flow projections based on the Company's financial projections presented to the Board covering a five-year period, and a discount rate of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;14&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; percent. Cash flows beyond that five-year period were extrapolated using the fifth-year data with no implied growth factor. The reporting unit level is defined as an operating segment or one level below an operating segment.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The recoverable amount of the intangible assets tested for impairment within the H&amp;amp;P Technologies reporting unit is determined based on undiscounted cash flow projections using the Company's financial projections presented to the Board covering a five-year period and extrapolated for the remaining weighted average useful lives of the intangible assets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The most significant assumptions used in our cash flow model include timing of awarded future contracts, commercial pricing terms, utilization, discount rate, and the terminal value. These assumptions are classified as Level 3 inputs by ASC Topic 820 Fair Value Measurement and Disclosures as they are based upon unobservable inputs and primarily rely on management assumptions and forecasts. Although we believe the assumptions used in our analysis and the probability-weighted average of expected future cash flows are reasonable and appropriate, different assumptions and estimates could materially impact the analysis and our resulting conclusion.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Impairment - Fiscal Year 2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;During the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2018, and as part of our annual goodwill impairment test, we performed a detailed assessment of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;TerraVici&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; reporting unit, where &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$4.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of goodwill was allocated. We determined that the estimated fair value of this reporting unit was less than its carrying amount and we recorded goodwill impairment losses of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$4.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. &#160;In addition, we recorded an intangible assets impairment loss of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$0.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. These impairment losses&#160;are &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#252525;"&gt;included&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in Asset Impairment Charge on the Consolidated Statements of Operations for the&#160;fiscal year ended September&#160;30, 2018. Our goodwill impairment analysis performed on our remaining technology reporting units in the fourth quarter of fiscal year 2018 did not result in an impairment charge.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;</us-gaap:GoodwillAndIntangibleAssetsDisclosureTextBlock>

style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"/&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;HPIDC 2025 Notes&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;On March 19, 2015, our subsidiary, HPIDC issued &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$500.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;4.65 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; unsecured senior notes due 2025 of HPIDC (the "HPIDC 2025 Notes"), which were redeemed in full on September 27, 2019 as described under "&#x2013;&#x2013;Exchange Offer, Consent Solicitation and Redemption."&#160;Interest on the HPIDC 2025 Notes was payable semi-annually on March 15 and September 15.&#160;The debt discount was being amortized to interest expense using the effective interest method.&#160;The debt issuance costs were being amortized straight-line over the stated life of the obligation, which approximated the effective interest method.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;Exchange Offer, Consent Solicitation and Redemption&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;On December 20, 2018, we settled an offer to exchange (the &#x201c;Exchange Offer&#x201d;) any and all outstanding HPIDC 2025 Notes for (i) up to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$500.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; aggregate principal amount of new &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;4.65 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; unsecured senior notes due 2025 of the Company (the &#x201c;Company 2025 Notes&#x201d;), with registration rights, and (ii) cash, pursuant to which we issued approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$487.1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in aggregate principal amount of Company 2025 Notes. Interest on the Company 2025 Notes is payable semi-annually on March 15 and September 15 of each year, commencing March 15, 2019. The debt issuance costs are being amortized straight-line over the stated life of the obligation, which approximates the effective interest method.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Following the consummation of the Exchange Offer, HPIDC had outstanding approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$12.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in aggregate principal amount of HPIDC 2025 Notes. On December 20, 2018, HPIDC, the Company and Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as trustee, entered into a supplemental indenture to the indenture governing the HPIDC 2025 Notes to adopt certain proposed amendments pursuant to a consent solicitation conducted concurrently with the Exchange Offer.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;On September 27, 2019, we redeemed the remaining approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$12.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in aggregate principal amount of HPIDC 2025 Notes for approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$14.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, including accrued interest and a prepayment premium. Simultaneously with the redemption of the HPIDC 2025 Notes, HPIDC was released as a guarantor under the Company 2025 Notes and the 2018 Credit Facility. As a result of such release, H&amp;amp;P is the only obligor under the Company 2025 Notes and the 2018 Credit Facility.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Credit Facilities&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;On November 13, 2018, we entered into a credit agreement by and among the Company, as borrower, Wells Fargo Bank, National Association, as administrative agent, and the lenders party thereto, which was amended on November 13, 2019, providing for an unsecured revolving credit facility (the &#x201c;2018 Credit Facility&#x201d;) that is set to mature on November 13, 2024. The 2018 Credit Facility has &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$750.0&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; million in aggregate availability with a maximum of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$75.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; available for use as letters of credit. The 2018 Credit Facility also permits aggregate commitments under the facility to be increased by &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$300.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, subject to the satisfaction of certain conditions and the procurement of additional commitments from new or existing lenders. The borrowings under the 2018 Credit Facility accrue interest at a spread over either the London Interbank Offered Rate ("LIBOR") or the Base Rate. We also pay a commitment fee on the unused balance of the facility. Borrowing spreads as well as commitment fees are determined based on the debt rating for senior unsecured debt of the Company, as determined by Moody&#x2019;s and Standard &amp;amp; Poor&#x2019;s. The spread over LIBOR ranges from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.875 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1.500 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; per annum and commitment fees range from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.075 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.200 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; per annum. Based on the unsecured debt rating of the Company on &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, the spread over LIBOR would have been &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1.125 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; had borrowings been outstanding under the 2018 Credit Facility and commitment fees are &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;0.125 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. There is a financial covenant in the 2018 Credit Facility that requires us to maintain a total debt to total capitalization ratio of less than or equal to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;50 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. The 2018 Credit Facility contains additional terms, conditions, restrictions and covenants that we believe are usual and customary in unsecured debt arrangements for companies of similar size and credit quality, including a limitation that priority debt (as defined in the credit agreement) may not exceed &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;17.5 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the net worth of the Company. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, there were &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Verdana,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;no&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; borrowings or letters of credit outstanding, leaving &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$750.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; available to borrow under the 2018 Credit Facility. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we had &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;two&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; separate outstanding letters of credit with banks, in the amounts of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$24.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we also had a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$20.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; unsecured standalone line of credit facility, for the purpose of obtaining the issuance of international letters of credit, bank guarantees, and performance bonds. Of the &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$20.0 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$4.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of financial guarantees were outstanding as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&#160;Subsequent to September 30, 2020, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; in financial guarantees have expired. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The applicable agreements for all unsecured debt contain additional terms, conditions and restrictions that we believe are usual and customary in unsecured debt arrangements for companies that are similar in size and credit quality.     <us-gaap:RevenueFromContractWithCustomerTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2020Q4YTD"
      id="TextSelection-FBEFD55527AFFF37C83F851D0E656445-0-wk-Fact-E022E13E4707F5575F51851D0E2410A0">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;NOTE 11 REVENUE FROM CONTRACTS WITH CUSTOMERS&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Drilling Services Revenue&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The majority of our drilling services are performed on a &#x201c;daywork&#x201d; contract basis, under which we charge a rate per day, with the price determined by the location, depth and complexity of the well to be drilled, operating conditions, the duration of the contract, and the competitive forces of the market. These drilling services, including our technology solutions, represent a series of distinct daily services that are substantially the same, with the same pattern of transfer to the customer. Because our customers benefit equally throughout the service period and our efforts in providing drilling services are incurred relatively evenly over the period of performance, revenue is recognized over time using a time-based input measure as we provide services to the customer.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Contracts generally contain renewal or extension provisions exercisable at the option of the customer at prices mutually agreeable to us and the customer. For contracts that are terminated by customers prior to the expirations of their fixed terms, contractual provisions customarily require early termination amounts to be paid to us. Revenues from early terminated contracts are recognized when all contractual requirements have been met.&#160;During the fiscal years ended September 30, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Verdana,sans-serif;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, early termination revenue associated with term contracts was approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$73.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$11.3 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$17.1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. During the fiscal years ended September 30, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2018&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, notification fee revenue related to well-to-well contracts was approximately &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$2.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$1.2 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$0.2 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&#160;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We also act as a principal for certain reimbursable services and auxiliary equipment provided by us to our clients, for which we incur costs and earn revenues. Many of these costs are variable, or dependent upon the activity that is performed each day under the related contract. Accordingly, reimbursements that we receive for out-of-pocket expenses are recorded as revenues and the out-of-pocket expenses for which they relate are recorded as operating costs during the period to which they relate within the series of distinct time increments. All of our revenues are recognized net of sales taxes, when applicable.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;With most drilling contracts, we also receive payments contractually designated for the mobilization and demobilization of drilling rigs and other equipment to and from the client&#x2019;s drill site. Revenues associated with the mobilization and demobilization of our drilling rigs to and from the client&#x2019;s drill site do not relate to a distinct good or service.  These revenues are deferred and recognized ratably over the related contract term that drilling services are provided.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Demobilization fees expected to be received upon contract completion are estimated at contract inception and recognized on a straight-line basis over the contract term. The amount of demobilization revenue that we ultimately collect is dependent upon the specific contractual terms, most of which include provisions for reduced or no payment for demobilization when, among other things, the contract is renewed or extended with the same client, or when the rig is subsequently contracted with another client prior to the termination of the current contract. Since revenues associated with demobilization activity are typically variable, at each period end, they are estimated at the most likely amount, and constrained when the likelihood of a significant reversal is probable. Any change in the expected amount of demobilization revenue is accounted for with the net cumulative impact of the change in estimate recognized in the period during which the revenue estimate is revised.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Contract Costs&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Mobilization costs include certain direct costs incurred for mobilization of contracted rigs. These costs relate directly to a contract, enhance resources that will be used in satisfying the future performance obligations and are expected to be recovered. These costs are capitalized when incurred and recorded as current or noncurrent contract fulfillment cost assets (depending on the length of the initial contract term), and are amortized on a systematic basis consistent with the pattern of the transfer of the goods or services to which the asset relates which typically includes the initial term of the related drilling contract or a period longer than the initial contract term if management anticipates a customer will renew or extend a contract, which we expect to benefit from the cost of mobilizing the rig. Abnormal mobilization costs are fulfillment costs that are incurred from excessive resources, wasted or spoiled materials, and unproductive labor costs that are not otherwise anticipated in the contract price and are expensed as incurred. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, we had capitalized fulfillment costs of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$6.2 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$13.9 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-align:justify;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;If capital modification&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;costs are incurred for rig modifications or if upgrades are required for a contract, these costs are considered to be capital improvements. These costs are capitalized as property, plant and equipment and depreciated over the estimated useful life of the improvement.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Remaining Performance Obligations&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The total aggregate transaction price allocated to the unsatisfied performance obligations, commonly referred to as backlog, as of&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;was approximately&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$670.1 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, of which &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$446.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; is expected to be recognized during fiscal year &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2021&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, and approximately&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$223.4 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#160;in fiscal year &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2022&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and thereafter. These amounts do not include anticipated contract renewals. Additionally, contracts that currently contain month-to-month terms are represented in our backlog as &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;one month&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of unsatisfied performance obligations. Our contracts are subject to cancellation or modification at the election of the customer; however, due to the level of capital deployed by our customers on underlying projects, we have not been materially adversely affected by contract cancellations or modifications in the past. However, the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic is inherently uncertain, and, as a result, the Company is unable to reasonably estimate the duration and ultimate impacts of the pandemic, including the effect it may have on our contractual obligations with our customers.  &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Contract Assets and Liabilities&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Amounts owed from our customers under our revenue contracts are typically billed on a monthly basis as the service is being provided and are due within &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;30 days&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of billing. Such amounts are classified as accounts receivable on our Consolidated Balance Sheets. Under certain of our contracts, we recognize revenues in excess of billings, referred to as contract assets, within prepaid expenses and other current assets within our Consolidated Balance Sheets.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Under certain of our contracts, we may be entitled to receive payments in advance of satisfying our performance obligations under the contract. We recognize a liability for these payments in excess of revenue recognized, referred to as deferred revenue or contract liabilities, within accrued liabilities and other noncurrent liabilities in our Consolidated Balance Sheets. Contract balances are presented at the net amount at a contract level.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span #000000;background-color:#cceeff;border-top:1px solid #000000;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:inherit;font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;br/&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:8px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:24px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;padding-left:0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;(1)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;The number of restricted stock awards granted includes phantom shares that confer the benefits of owning company stock without the actual ownership or transfer of any shares. There were &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;20,616&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt; phantom shares granted during fiscal year &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:8px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:24px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;padding-left:0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;(2)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;The number of restricted stock awards vested includes shares that we withheld on behalf of our employees to satisfy the statutory tax withholding requirements.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:16px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-style:italic;"&gt;Performance Share Units&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We have made awards to certain employees that are subject to market-based performance conditions ("performance share units"). Subject to the terms and conditions set forth in the applicable performance share unit award agreements and the 2016 Plan, grants of performance share units are subject to a vesting period of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; (the &#x201c;Vesting Period&#x201d;) that is dependent on the achievement of certain performance goals. Such performance share unit awards consist of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;two&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; separate components.&#160;Performance share units that comprise the first component are subject to a &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance cycle.&#160;Performance share units that comprise the second component are further divided into &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; separate tranches, each of which is subject to a separate &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;one&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance cycle within the full &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;three&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;-year performance cycle.&#160;&#160;The vesting of the performance share units is generally dependent on (i) the achievement of the Company&#x2019;s total shareholder return (&#x201c;TSR&#x201d;) performance goals relative to the TSR achievement of a peer group of companies (the &#x201c;Peer Group&#x201d;) over the applicable performance cycle, and (ii) the continued employment of the recipient of the performance share unit award throughout the Vesting Period.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;At the end of the Vesting Period, recipients receive dividend equivalents, if any, with respect to the number of vested performance share units. The vesting of units ranges from &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;zero&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; to &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;200 percent&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of the units granted depending on the Company&#x2019;s TSR relative to the TSR of the Peer Group on the vesting date.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The grant date fair value of performance share units was determined through use of the Monte Carlo simulation method. The Monte Carlo simulation method requires the use of highly subjective assumptions. Our key assumptions in the method include the price and the expected volatility of our stock and our self-determined Peer Group companies' stock, risk free rate of return and cross-correlations between the Company and our Peer Group companies. The valuation model assumes dividends are immediately reinvested. As of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, there was &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$6.6 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; of unrecognized compensation cost related to unvested performance share units. That cost is expected to be recognized over a weighted-average period of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;1.9 years&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;A summary of the status of our performance share units as of &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and changes in non-vested performance share units outstanding during the fiscal year ended &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span     <us-gaap:EarningsPerShareTextBlock
      contextRef="FD2020Q4YTD"
      id="TextSelection-FBEB7CDBE93BBBF117E1851D0E66CFB7-0-wk-Fact-468B2887D280BBC92BFA851D0D94D29E">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:0px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;NOTE 13 EARNINGS (LOSSES) PER COMMON SHARE&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;ASC 260, Earnings per Share, requires companies to treat unvested share-based payment awards that have non-forfeitable rights to dividends or dividend equivalents as a separate class of securities in calculating earnings per share.&#160;&#160;We have granted and expect to continue to grant to employees restricted stock grants that contain non-forfeitable rights to dividends.&#160;Such grants are considered participating securities under ASC 260.&#160;&#160;As such, we are required to include these grants in the calculation of our basic earnings per share and calculate basic earnings per share using the two-class method. The two-class method of computing earnings per share is an earnings allocation formula that determines earnings per share for each class of common stock and participating security according to dividends declared (or&#160;accumulated) and participation rights in undistributed earnings.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Basic earnings per share is computed utilizing the two-class method and is calculated based on the weighted-average number of common shares outstanding during the periods presented.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Diluted earnings per share is computed using the weighted-average number of common and common equivalent shares outstanding during the periods utilizing the two-class method for stock options, nonvested restricted stock and performance share units.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Under the two-class method of calculating earnings per share, dividends paid and a portion of undistributed net income, but not losses, are allocated to unvested restricted stock grants that receive dividends, which are considered participating securities.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The following table sets forth the computation of basic and diluted earnings per share:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div       id="TextSelection-64A4066E4D8C4BB46583851D0E67CB0F-0-wk-Fact-44CFEF19E5BD2DEFFB44851D0E081C9F">&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;padding-left:60px;text-indent:-60px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt;NOTE 14 FAIR VALUE MEASUREMENT OF FINANCIAL INSTRUMENTS&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;font-weight:bold;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;We have certain assets and liabilities that are required to be measured and disclosed at fair value. Fair value is defined as the exchange price that would be received to sell an asset or paid to transfer a liability (an exit price) in the principal or most advantageous market for the asset or liability in an orderly transaction between market participants at the measurement date.&#160;&#160;We use the fair value hierarchy established in ASC 820-10 to measure fair value to prioritize the inputs:&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:13px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;text-align:left;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Level&#160;1 &#x2014; Quoted prices (unadjusted) in active markets for identical assets or liabilities that the reporting entity can access at the measurement date.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Level&#160;2 &#x2014; Observable inputs, other than quoted prices included in Level 1, such as quoted prices for similar assets or liabilities in active markets; quoted prices for similar assets and liabilities in markets that are not active; or other inputs that are observable or can be corroborated by observable market data.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:96px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;padding-left:72px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&#x2022;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Level&#160;3 &#x2014; Unobservable inputs that are supported by little or no market activity and that are significant to the fair value of the assets or liabilities.&#160;&#160;This includes pricing models, discounted cash flow methodologies and similar techniques that use significant unobservable inputs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The assets held in a Non-Qualified Supplemental Savings Plan are carried at fair value and totaled &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$19.8 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span&gt;$15.7 million&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; at &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;September&#160;30, 2020&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt; and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;, respectively. The assets are comprised of mutual funds that are measured using Level 1 inputs.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Short-term investments include securities classified as trading securities.&#160;&#160;Both realized and unrealized gains and losses on trading securities are included in other income (expense) in the Consolidated Statements of Operations.&#160;&#160;The securities are recorded at fair value.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Our non-financial assets, such as intangible assets, goodwill and property, plant and equipment, are recorded at fair value when acquired in a business combination or when an impairment charge is recognized.&#160;If measured at fair value in the Consolidated Balance Sheets, these would generally be classified within Level 2 or 3 of the fair value hierarchy. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The majority of cash equivalents are invested in highly-liquid money-market mutual funds invested primarily in direct or indirect obligations of the U.S. Government and in federally insured deposit accounts. The carrying amount of cash and cash equivalents approximates fair value due to the short maturity of those investments.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div and &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;2019&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="vertical-align:bottom;padding-right:2px;padding-top:2px;padding-bottom:2px;"&gt;&lt;div style="text-align:left;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;%&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;table cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" style="padding-top:8px;font-family:Times New Roman; font-size:10pt;"&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="width:24px;"/&gt;&lt;td/&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;tr&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;padding-left:0px;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;(1)&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;td style="vertical-align:top;"&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;font-size:8pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:8pt;"&gt;The weighted average of the payment amounts and the probabilities (Level 3 unobservable inputs), associated with the contingent consideration valued using probability analysis, were weighted by the relative undiscounted fair value of payment amounts and of probability payment amounts, respectively. &lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;/td&gt;&lt;/tr&gt;&lt;/table&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The above significant unobservable inputs are subject to change based on changes in economic and market conditions.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;font-style:italic;"&gt; &lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;The use of significant unobservable inputs creates uncertainty in the measurement of fair value as of the reporting date. The significant unobservable inputs used in the fair value measurement of the contingent consideration using Monte Carlo simulation are (i)&#160;discount rate, (ii)&#160;revenue volatility and (iii) risk-free rate. Significant increases or decreases in the discount rate and risk-free rate in isolation would result in a significantly lower or higher fair value measurement. Significant changes in revenue volatility in isolation would result in a significantly lower or higher fair value measurement. The significant unobservable inputs used in the fair value measurement of the contingent consideration using probability analysis are (i)&#160;discount rate, (ii)&#160;payment amounts and (iii) probabilities. Significant increases or decreases in the discount rate in isolation would result in a significantly lower or higher fair value measurement. Significant increases or decreases in the payment amounts or probabilities in isolation would result in a significantly higher or lower fair value measurement. It is not possible for us to predict the effect of future economic or market conditions on our estimated fair values.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;color:#212529;font-style:italic;"&gt;&#160;&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span Allocation&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div style="line-height:120%;padding-top:13px;text-indent:48px;font-size:9pt;"&gt;&lt;span style="font-family:Arial;font-size:9pt;"&gt;Our investment policy and strategies are established with a long-term view in mind.&#160;The investment strategy is intended to help pay the cost of the Pension Plan while providing adequate security to meet the benefits promised under the Pension Plan.&#160;We maintain a diversified asset mix to minimize the risk of a material loss to the portfolio value that might occur from devaluation of any single investment.&#160;In determining the appropriate asset mix, our financial strength and ability to fund potential shortfalls are considered.&#160;Pension Plan assets are invested in portfolios of diversified public-market equity securities and fixed income securities.&#160;The Pension Plan does not directly hold securities of the Company.&lt;/span&gt;&lt;/div&gt;&lt;div on historical and projected rates of return for current and planned asset classes in the Pension Plan&#x2019;s investment portfolio after analyzing historical experience and future expectations of the <table border="0" cellpadding="0" cellspacing="0" class="authRefData" style="display: none;" id="defref_us-gaap_StockholdersEquity">
<tr><td class="hide"><a style="color: white;" href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.hideAR();">X</a></td></tr>
<tr><td><div class="body" style="padding: 2px;">
<a href="javascript:void(0);" onclick="top.Show.toggleNext( this );">- Definition</a><div><p>Total of all stockholders' equity (deficit) items, net of receivables from officers, directors, owners, and affiliates of the entity which are attributable to the parent. The amount of the economic entity's stockholders' equity attributable to the parent excludes the amount of stockholders' equity which is allocable to that ownership interest in subsidiary equity which is not attributable to the parent (noncontrolling interest, minority interest). This excludes temporary equity and is sometimes called permanent equity.</p></div>
